set.descent_text: The route finishes with a traverse across the top of the tower, where the way down is the rappel line of the Northeast Face. Carry two ropes for it, and expect loose rock around the first stations.

review.notes: East Face Left page says the Northeast Face rappel route is the way down; NE Face page for the rope and loose-rock facts. No rappel count given.

set.descent_text: The usual way down is to rappel the route with two ropes (a single long rope runs out of length at some stations). One rappel traverses south across a slab into a chimney to regain the line, and the first rappel has loose rock on the ledge below, so pull the ropes carefully. A fixed station on the ridge below the headwall pitch can serve as an intermediate rappel point. A walk-off toward the Warbonnet side is loose, slow and best avoided, with a couloir that can hold steep snow early in the season.

review.notes: Single page; no rappel count stated.

set.descent_text: Descend by rappel. The rappels are long and need two long ropes. Loose blocks and flakes near the stations make pulling the ropes risky, so clear the lines and watch for snags.
set.approach: Follow the Wolf's Head trail where it splits off to the south of Pingora, then work along the base of the formation on a slabby, flower-covered ramp. A little class 4 traversing leads to the start, which sits directly beneath the thumb-shaped spire on the wall.

review.notes: Single route page for location and rappel descent; rope count and number of rappels left out (one source).
